name: Kai M. Siegbahn
summary: Swedish physicist who developed X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS/ESCA) and won the Nobel Prize in Physics.

name: Uppsala University
summary: Swedish university where Siegbahn conducted seminal XPS work.

name: Stockholm
summary: Capital city of Sweden where Siegbahn started building his instrument.

name: Carl Nordling
summary: Graduate student and co-author with Siegbahn on the first accurate XPS spectrum.

name: Evelyn Sokolowski
summary: Graduate student and co-author with Siegbahn on the first chemical shift report.

name: David Shirley
summary: Pioneer in photoelectron spectroscopy who hosted Siegbahn for a sabbatical.

name: University of California, Berkeley
summary: University where Shirley's laboratory was located.

name: David Briggs
summary: Researcher who conducted a notable interview with Siegbahn.

name: Nobel Prize in Physics
summary: Prestigious award received by Siegbahn for his work on electron spectroscopy.

name: ESCA: Atomic, Molecular and Solid State Structure Studied by means of Electron Spectroscopy
summary: Seminal book by Siegbahn et al. focused on solids that marketed ESCA technique.

name: ESCA applied to free molecules
summary: Book by Siegbahn et al. concerned with gas phase ESCA.

name: U.S. Air Force Materials Laboratory
summary: Laboratory that hosted Siegbahn as a visitor and sponsored his work.
